q-24424.name: Question 1
q-24424.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the product rule for logarithms:

$$
{log}_{n}⁡a+{log}_{n}⁡b={log}_{n}⁡(ab)
$$

Using the product rule for logarithms, we can combine the first two terms as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡2+{log}_{5}⁡4+{log}_{5}⁡6 & ={log}_{5}⁡(2\cdot 4)+{log}_{5}⁡6 \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡8+{log}_{5}⁡6\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule for logarithms once more, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡8+{log}_{5}⁡6 & ={log}_{5}⁡(8\cdot 6) \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡48.\end{aligned}
$$

Express log5⁡2+log5⁡4+log5⁡6 as a single logarithm.

a
log5⁡10
b
log125⁡48
c
log15⁡48
d
log15⁡12
e
log5⁡48
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's recall the product rule for logarithms:

logn⁡a+logn⁡b=logn⁡(ab)

Using the product rule for logarithms, we can combine the first two terms as follows: log5⁡2+log5⁡4+log5⁡6=log5⁡(2⋅4)+log5⁡6=log5⁡8+log5⁡6

Using the product rule for logarithms once more, we obtain log5⁡8+log5⁡6=log5⁡(8⋅6)=log5⁡48.

Write the following expression as a single logarithm.

$5\operatorname{ln}⁡p+5\operatorname{ln}⁡q+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(pq)=5\operatorname{ln}⁡(${{field-1}}$)$

First, let's recall the product rule for logarithms:

$$
{log}_{n}⁡a+{log}_{n}⁡b={log}_{n}⁡(ab)

If we factor the given expression and use the product rule for logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{ln}⁡p+5\operatorname{ln}⁡q+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(pq) & =5(\operatorname{ln}⁡p+\operatorname{ln}⁡q+\operatorname{ln}⁡(pq)) \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(p\cdot q\cdot pq) \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡({p}^{2}{q}^{2}).\end{aligned}

logn⁡a+logn⁡b=logn⁡(ab)

Therefore, log2⁡(32x2)=log2⁡32+log2⁡(x2)=5+log2⁡(x2).
